title: Crisis command: 1990s Japanese mecha anime's crisis-terminal grammar - type cards in heavy compressed Mincho on black, red hexagon alarm walls, amber segment clocks, coupling graphs and a five-seat vote
summary: Two kinds of screen with two light regimes. Type cards: an almost black ground (79-97% dark) carrying one heavy Mincho block, the episode number at half the title's size, the title broken into an L (one glyph, then the rest after a half-pitch comma), nothing else. Alarm screens: a hot field (14-32% red-orange or amber) of elongated hexagon panels (3.06:1, 55-degree tips) in double rules over a 45-degree lattice, square two-character stamps, compressed English under the CJK, segment-digit clocks with Mincho units at 0.21 of the digit, mode rows with one lit cell. One hot colour family per screen; state changes are hard cuts.

provenance.case: tidemark (潮位警报 TIDEMARK): an original organisation terminal site in this grammar - six screens (title card, alarm wall, countdown, coupling and vote, episode-card index, frame archive with image slots), a 390-wide page, a ?slot=1 placeholder mode with image-generation task sheets - plus two in-app screens (operator console, sortie coupling monitor), and the crisis-command UI kit under examples/crisis-command-ui-kit.
provenance.lineage: The crisis-terminal and title-card grammar of 1990s Japanese mecha anime. Read and measured on frames and title cards collected for a private study (glyph ink boxes for the compression steps, palettes, whole-screen light and colour shares, frame-by-frame luminance of the countdown states); the frames stay private and are not shipped. Borrowed: the grammar and the measured proportions. Never borrowed: any name, logo, organisation, mark, character, mecha, line of dialogue, proprietary font or picture.
provenance.borrow: Borrow grammar, never assets. Every name, term and line in the case and the templates is our own (潮位警报, 环海闸务局, 闸甲, 闸手, 五席表决, 耦合率, 蓄压); the heavy Mincho is the open Noto Serif SC Black compressed with a transform, never the proprietary face; digits are drawn segments; mecha and pilots are image slots with task sheets, never drawn in code.
provenance.rounds: template check --browser on the case's pages (six screens at 1920 x 1080, the 390-wide page, two in-app screens) and the kit's previews: first pass and final counts in the PR.

fonts.substitution: The reference's title face is a proprietary heavy Mincho (EB weight). Noto Serif SC Black is the open substitute: fonts query --style mincho returns it first with full simplified coverage; Zen Old Mincho Black is closer in feel (soft brush corners, thick horizontals) but covers 64% of the 3,500 common simplified characters. Differences: the original's horizontals are thicker (about 1:2.5 against the stems) and its corners and scales rounder; Noto's horizontals are thinner and its scales sharper, so the film title stops at 0.40 instead of the measured 0.35.

grammar: Two light regimes: a type card is 79-97% black with one block of type (16-19% of the frame on a card, 3-9% on a film title), weighted to the lower left (0.38, 0.60) or the centre; an alarm screen is a hot field, 14-32% red-orange or amber, weighted to the centre.

Heavy Mincho is compressed mechanically, never redrawn: 1.00 on a title card, 0.85 in a caption and on a panel, 0.65 in credits, 0.35 (0.40 with the open face) on a film title; Latin under it is compressed too (0.45-0.9). One screen uses at most two steps.

The title card: margins H/24 (left 6.5% of H, top 6.4%), the number line at 15.4% of H ink (half the title), the title at 31% of H ink in two lines 3.3% apart: line one carries one glyph, line two the rest after a comma at half pitch.

Alarm panels are elongated hexagons, 3.06:1 with 55-degree tips, filled red at 86-92% over the lattice, ruled twice (6 and 2 units, 12 apart); square stamps of two Mincho characters in a double frame sit inside them.

Clocks are segment digits (capsule 0.36 wide per digit with its gap, or slanted LCD), units in Mincho at 0.21 of the digit, labels in vertical brackets at 0.27; a mode row of equal cells with one lit, a danger cell that fills red.
One hot colour family per screen (red-orange or amber); white and black are structure. Scale contrast of 1:10 or more on every screen (the clock against its smallest caption is about 1:23).
English sits under or beside the CJK, never above; no ornaments between them.

procedural: hexagon panels, stamps, hazard stripes, the 45-degree lattice and CRT scanlines (layouts-crisis.cjs)
the placeholder mark: three sluice bars over a water line (no letter shapes)
recipes: Screen grain under a panel: materials generate --generator halftone --params '{"periodPx":3,"angleDeg":0,"coverage":0.3}' --seed 1, laid at 10-14% over screens only, never over a type card.

Mecha, pilots and city views come from an image-generation task sheet (#311) with a painted-in blend (grade to the screen colour, a hot rim from the alarm side); until then the slot shows its size and safe box. Never draw them in code (#301).
collage: No pictures on type cards. On screens, pictures sit inside a framed monitor with a ground plate under any text.
materials.sources: Everything is drawn; pictures are your own art in image slots.

grammar: State changes are hard cuts (one frame): the measured danger switch doubles the red share (7% to 18%, 15% to 46%) and darkens the screen.
A live screen shimmers at low amplitude: a 2-3% luminance flicker every 80-150 ms (measured 6.7 Hz at 2/255 and frame-alternating 12.5 Hz at 2.4%), never a flash.
Title cards cut in from black, hold about 2 s and cut out; no fades.
Alarm bands blink at 1 Hz (our value, under 3 flashes a second); a scan band crosses the screen top to bottom in 4 s; clocks tick every second and the last 10 s cut to the danger red.
motion.flashLimit: No more than 3 flashes a second; the only large-area blink is the 1 Hz alarm band.

guidance: 64 px distinctiveness (guidance): shrink each screen to 64 px tall beside the other packs and the private reference thumbnails; a card should read as a white L of blocks on black, an alarm screen as a red honeycomb on blue, a clock as amber bars on black.
Never draw mecha, weapons or people in code (#301): leave an image slot with a task sheet; show mode uses type, frames, digits and stamps only.
Keep the compression steps: a line that needs less than 0.65 to fit is too long; cut the copy instead of squeezing further.
Latin roles take Latin, digits and ASCII punctuation only; mixed copy goes in head or body (glyph coverage).
Digits are drawn segments: clock slots take digits and the separators shown in their example; words go in a text slot.
